title: Parallel Lines and Transversals
seo_title: Parallel Lines and Transversals Worksheet (Geometry, G-CO.C.9) | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment's endpoints.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on parallel lines cut by a transversal: corresponding, alternate interior and same-side interior angles, solving for x, and proving lines parallel. 100 questions.
key_big: Parallel lines: corresponding and alternate angles are congruent.
key_sub: Same-side interior angles add to 180°. The converses prove lines parallel.
body_html:
How it works

A transversal crosses two lines and makes eight angles. When the two lines are parallel:

  • Corresponding angles (same position) are congruent.
  • Alternate interior angles (between the lines, opposite sides) are congruent.
  • Alternate exterior angles (outside the lines, opposite sides) are congruent.
  • Same-side interior angles (between the lines, same side) add to 180°.

Shortcut: every acute angle in the picture is equal, every obtuse angle is equal, and an acute plus an obtuse is 180°.

The converses are also true: if corresponding angles are congruent (or same-side interior angles are supplementary), the lines are parallel.

Example

ℓ ∥ m. Alternate interior angles are (4x + 6)° and (6x − 30)°. Find x.

Alternate interior angles are congruent: 4x + 6 = 6x − 30

36 = 2x

Answer: x = 18

Example

ℓ ∥ m. Same-side interior angles are (3x)° and (2x + 30)°. Find both angles.

They add to 180: 5x + 30 = 180, x = 30

Answer: 90° and 90°

Common mistakes

  • Setting same-side interior angles equal. They add to 180°.
  • Mixing up alternate interior (opposite sides) and same-side interior (same side).
  • Using these rules when the lines are not marked parallel.
  • Using vertical angles to prove lines parallel. Vertical angles are always congruent, so they prove nothing.

faq.a: Angles between the two lines and on opposite sides of the transversal. When the lines are parallel, they are congruent.
No. When the lines are parallel, same-side interior angles are supplementary: they add to 180 degrees.

faq.q: How do you prove two lines are parallel?
faq.a: Show that a pair of corresponding, alternate interior or alternate exterior angles is congruent, or that same-side interior angles are supplementary.
Angles in the same relative position at each intersection, such as both above the line and to the right of the transversal.

items.q: Lines ℓ and m are parallel. Find x.
items.e: Draw a line through the bend, parallel to ℓ and m. It splits x into two parts that are alternate interior angles with 44° and 30°. So x = 44 + 30 = 74.

items.q: The handrail of a staircase is parallel to the line of the stairs. The stairs make a 34° angle with the floor. The handrail post is vertical. What acute angle does the handrail make with the post?
items.e: The handrail makes a 34° angle with the horizontal (corresponding angles). The post is vertical, at 90° to the horizontal, so the angle between the rail and the post is 90° − 34° = 56°.

items.e: Same-side interior angles with parallel lines are supplementary: 180° − 69° = 111°.
